text: If someone's offering is a fellowship sacrifice, if he brings it from the herd, whether male or female, he must present one without defect before the LORD.

versions.text: If someone's offering is a fellowship sacrifice, and he brings an animal from the herd, whether male or female, he must present one without defect before the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two conditional clauses ('if... if from the herd'), not 'and'. Also 'an animal' is added; the object is already the offering. Keeping 'it from the herd' is closer to the Hebrew and reads smoothly.

versions.text: If someone's offering is a fellowship sacrifice, and he brings it from the herd, whether male or female, he must present one without defect before the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has a second conditional particle (אִם מִן־הַבָּקָר), so the clause is 'if he brings it from the herd' rather than a coordinated 'and'. This was the stated intent of the earlier revision, but the connective itself was left as 'and'; the conditional reading also matches the parallel structure in verses 6 and 12. The existing wording is understandable and reads smoothly, so it remains a defensible alternative.

text: He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of meeting; then Aaron's sons, the priests, shall splash the blood against the altar on all sides.

versions.text: He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons, the priests, shall splash the blood against all sides of the altar.
versions.explanation: Breaking the long sentence with a semicolon and 'then' improves oral rhythm, and 'against the altar on all sides' renders סָבִיב more naturally than 'against all sides of the altar'.

text: From the fellowship sacrifice he shall present as a food offering to the LORD the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
and the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove along with the kidneys.

versions.text: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove along with the kidneys.
versions.explanation: The verse continues the list from verse 3, so an opening 'and' aids the flow when read aloud; 'the two kidneys' also matches שְׁתֵּי הַכְּלָיֹת.

text: Then Aaron's sons shall burn it on the altar, on top of the burnt offering that lies on the wood over the fire—a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If his offering to the LORD for a fellowship sacrifice comes from the flock, he must present a male or female without defect.
If he offers a lamb, he shall bring it before the LORD,
lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons shall splash its blood against all sides of the altar.

From the fellowship sacrifice he shall present as a food offering to the LORD its fat: the entire fat tail, which he shall remove close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails, and all the fat that is on the entrails,

versions.text: From the fellowship sacrifice he shall present as a food offering to the LORD its fat: the entire fat tail, cut off close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb יְסִירֶנָּה is an active future ('he shall remove it'), matching the parallel wording in verses 4, 10 and 15; 'cut off' obscures the verb. A comma before 'and all the fat' also aids reading.

text: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove along with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn it on the altar as food, an offering made by fire to the LORD.

versions.text: The priest shall burn it on the altar as food, a food offering to the LORD.
versions.explanation: 'as food, a food offering' is repetitive and confusing when heard aloud, since לֶחֶם ('food/bread') and אִשֶּׁה ('fire offering') are distinct terms. Distinguishing them clarifies the sense.

text: If his offering is a goat, he shall present it before the LORD,
lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons shall splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
From it he shall present his offering as a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove along with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to the LORD.

versions.text: The priest shall burn them on the altar as food, a food offering, a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
versions.explanation: As in verse 11, 'as food, a food offering' is redundant to the ear; distinguishing לֶחֶם from אִשֶּׁה makes the line clearer for oral reading.

text: This is a lasting statute for your generations, wherever you live: you must not eat any fat or any blood.
